prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: Across frames 1–4, the harmonium, open book, camera wearer's forearms and hands form the nearest central cluster, roughly 0.3–0.8 m away; the bottles sit beyond them near the upper-left/upper-centre at about 1–2 m, while walls and furniture are farther behind. The book lies above and slightly behind the keyboard, the bottles stand behind and left of the book, and the wearer's hands remain within arm's reach and partly occlude the instrument. In frame 5, a second person enters very close in front of the wearer, about 0.3–0.8 m away, filling the centre-left and occluding most of the instrument; the depth map makes this sharp approach clearer than RGB. Absolute metre estimates and boundaries around the hands, book, and close person are unreliable because monocular depth is scale-ambiguous, and the person's distance appears uneven across their body.
descriptions.segmentation: Frames 1–4 consistently isolate an open book near the centre, three or four bottles behind it toward the upper-left, and parts of a person near the bottom or right edge; the book is roughly 0.4–0.8 m from the wearer and the bottles roughly 1–2 m away. The masks clarify that the book is in front of and below the bottles, while the visible person regions are closer to the wearer and partly out of frame; however, the map does not distinguish the camera wearer's arms from another person's body, so ownership and inter-person distances remain uncertain. The person's mask shifts from the lower-right edge in frame 1 to lower-centre in frame 2, is smaller near the bottom in frame 3, and extends across the lower-right in frame 4, consistent with changing arm position rather than a reliable whole-body trajectory. Frame 5 has no useful masks even though RGB shows a nearby person occluding the scene, and several instrument, furniture, hand, and bottle regions are missed or inconsistently separated, making depth, facing direction, gaze, and occlusion order hard to infer from segmentation alone.
descriptions.pose: The pose map detects only hand skeletons: two separated hands in frames 1, 3, and 4, one hand in frame 2, and none in frame 5; no reliable body skeleton is visible, so whole-person location, facing direction, gaze, and distance cannot be recovered. In frames 1–4, the hands lie low in front of the wearer over the instrument, approximately 0.3–0.7 m away and within the wearer's arm's reach; one is left of centre and the other is nearer the centre or right, with the right-side hand rotating and shifting rightward by frame 4. The skeletons reveal finger and palm orientation more clearly than RGB despite partial occlusion by the keyboard and book, but they do not establish whether every detected hand belongs to the camera wearer. The close person entering in frame 5 occludes most of the working area and is not detected, while missing joints, distorted finger geometry, and the absence of body landmarks make the map unreliable for inter-person spacing or approach and retreat beyond that occlusion.
